habitat: When not breeding, flocks can be very large, in grassland, bushveld and farmlands. They go to water in the evenings.
summary: A very common resident. It looks black at a distance. The adult has a blue neck, a red cap and a horny casque. The chick is buffy-brown with darker stripes. The juvenile is mostly brown, darker above, and keeps head-stripes until the casque starts to grow. The immature resembles the adult but has a feathered neck, a dark brown helmet and a rudimentary casque. The usual call is ker-bek-ker-bek-ker-bek, krrrrrr. The female also gives a continual piping t-phueet. The Kemp code RB was left unchanged.

similar.note: Southern Crested Guineafowl is blacker, with black head-plumes and an unmarked black neck, not a blue neck and a casque.
